items.title: The judge who made room for the young
items.summary: There are judges whose legacy is measured in landmark judgments they had delivered while in office and there are judges whose contribution is remembered through constitutional principles that continue to shape the law long after they have left the bench. And then there are judges whose legacy lies in something less visible, but perhaps equally important in terms of the people they encouraged, the confidence they instilled in others and the opportunities they created. Justice Sanjay Karol , who retires from the Supreme Court today, belongs to that last category in a way that deserves to be remembered. I say this not merely as an observer of the Court, but as someone who had the opportunity, in the early days of my clerkship (July to September 2025) at the Supreme Court, to sit in his courtroom. The judge under whom I am clerking was bench partner with Justice Karol during the relevant time. What stayed with me from his Court was not one particular judgment or one particular exchange. Rather, it was the atmosphere of the courtroom itself. It was a young lawyer’s courtroom. In an institution where experience understandably commands respect, Justice Karol’s courtroom seemed to be operating on a slightly different principle: experience deserved respect, but youth deserved an opportunity. A junior who had just begun appearing before the Supreme Court was not treated as someone who had to wait for years before being heard. The nervous first submission, the imperfect argument and the unfamiliarity with the courtroom - none of these actually became reasons to shut the door, especially in the courtroom of Justice Karol. Instead, they often became reasons to open it. Justice Karol would ask senior advocates why their juniors were not arguing. He would also notice the younger members of the Bar and give them time. When a young lawyer made a good submission, he acknowledged the youngster for his arguments. At the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) farewell held ahead of his retirement , Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant spoke precisely of this quality itself. He recalled how Justice Karol would tell senior advocates when their juniors had argued a matter well, observing that such encouragement from a senior judge could mean far more to a young lawyer than any reassurance from elsewhere. The Bench said Pandey’s claim of personality rights in the suit may be overly broad. It stressed that the Court’s duty is to ensure that such cases are not misused for getting orders to take down legally permissible forms of expression. Ltd. vs. Baby Gift House and Others , this court would want to examine and ensure that personality rights are not deployed to prevent dissemination of information in relation to wrongdoing; or to extinguish an entire genre of expression including caricature, lampooning or parody which may not amount to commercial exploitation of an individual’s personality or publicity rights,” Justice Bhambhani said. items.title: Whether SG, ASG or junior counsel, our order will be the same: Supreme Court rejects adjournment request
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Saturday dismissed a plea after declining to adjourn the matter merely because the Additional Solicitor General (ASG) appearing in the case was held up in another courtroom. A Bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva made it clear that the seniority or designation of the advocate appearing made no difference to how the Court would decide a case. This was after government counsel sought adjournment in the matter, stating that ASG is on his legs in another court. "Learned ASG is held up in some other court. Please have it on Monday or Tuesday. Let him be there," the counsel said. “Whether ASG, Solicitor General, our order will be the same. It does not differ based on the advocates who appear before us. Please tell your ASG that. If Mr. Senior counsel will appear, we will pass another order? In our court, every counsel is the same,” Justice Nagarathna said. Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva Justice BV Nagarathna Whether ASG, SG, our order will be the same. It does not differ based on the advocates who appear before us. Please tell your ASG that. The judge added that the Court does not treat lawyers differently based on their designation, and that what mattered to it was the quality of assistance rendered, not the gown worn. She also noted that that the Court is sometimes more frustrated by senior counsel who offer only noise and little assistance. “We look at the gown and say senior counsel or not. Sometimes we say senior counsel, they only say we are not senior counsel. Everybody is the same to us. A junior may assist, we give the best order then. We feel satisfied. If a junior assists very well. But we feel frustrated when a senior doesn’t assist well. Sometimes it’s just noise and no assistance,” Justice Nagarathna remarked.

items.title: Chennai Dalit man hacked to death for falling in love, demand for anti-honour killing law rises
items.summary: A 23-year-old Dalit man was brutally hacked to death in yet another ‘honour’ killing in Tamil Nadu. Praveen Kumar, who was attacked with machetes on the night of August 16, succumbed to his injuries on August 20 at the Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital (RGGH) in Chennai. Praveen, who belonged to a Scheduled Caste community, was a resident of Kelambakkam in Chengalpattu district, very near to Chennai. Kelambakkam T-19 police have identified the perpetrators as Manikandan, Ezhumalai, Nantheesh, and Gautham. All four were arrested and sent to judicial custody on August 17. A search is underway for a fifth accused who is absconding, police also said. Ezhumalai is a member of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), according to multiple news reports, triggering further anger among anti-caste activists. Allegedly, Praveen and Ezhumalai’s daughter, Ashwathi, had been romantically interested in each other. Not the first instance of violence According to Sathish Kumar, a neighbour, both Praveen and Ezhumalai are from the Scheduled Caste (SC) Adi Dravidar community. However, Praveen is from a far poorer family, Sathish added. He further alleged that Praveen has been threatened multiple times. “On a previous occasion, one of Ashwathi’s relatives came armed to Praveen's house. He shouted, threatened and even lunged at Praveen with a knife. Then he went away. There have been continuous threats.” Around six months ago, Sathish alleged, Praveen was tied and beaten up by Ezhumalai and the other accused. At the time, Praveen’s family ultimately decided not to file a police report, Sathish said. He added that Manikandan, one of the accused, had struck up a friendship with Praveen about three months back. On the day of the murder, Praveen allegedly went to meet Manikandan, after which he was abducted in a car and taken away to where he was attacked. Special law against ‘honour’ killings This is not the first ‘honour killing’ case in or near Chennai in the recent past. In March 2024, another victim, also named Praveen (22), was murdered for his marriage to Sharmilla, a Yadava (OBC) woman. Until March this year, at least 59 honour killings have been committed in Tamil Nadu. Activists have repeatedly said that the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, or PoA Act, is insufficient to curb such killings. items.title: 59 DMK MLAs reject Tamil Nadu government cars citing state’s financial situation
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Leader of the Opposition, Udhayanidhi Stalin on Friday, August 21, said that all 59 Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MLAs will not accept the new cars considering the government’s statement that the state finances were not good. Earlier, Chief Minister Joseph Vijay had announced in the Assembly that all the legislators would receive a car and Rs 75,000 monthly vehicle allowance for constituency-related work. Udhayanidhi said, “DMK members do not need government cars. Cars should be given to those who are struggling, taking into account the state's economic situation. The vehicles should be given (to MLAs) after looking at the assets' value mentioned in the election affidavit.” Referring to the government’s allegation that the treasury was empty, Udhayanidhi said, "From the day the government assumed office, the allegation has been that the treasury is empty. The DMK’s stand is that cars are not needed. Let them buy cars for those who need them." He also added that the decision was taken in the direction of former Chief Minister MK Stalin. Minister Aadhav Arjuna said the cars would help the MLAs meet people in their constituencies. “Many newly elected MLAs come from humble backgrounds. There is an MLA from Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) who travels by public bus. This initiative ensures equality." VCK MLA LE Jothimani from the Kattumannarkoil constituency requested a car from the state government. Hitting back at Udayanidhi, Aadhav said he was living in an official government residence despite owning multiple bungalows. DMK MLA KN Nehru pointed out that as Leader of Opposition, Udhayanidhi was allowed to avail government accommodation, as he has a cabinet-rank post. Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) leader Sowmiya Anbumani said that the money could be used to build paddy procurement centres, and two of their MLAs would not take the cars. Communist Party of India (CPI) floor leader T Ramachandran also said that the party would turn down the cars. This story was written by a student interning with TNM.
